state: A regional telecom operator's service-assurance analytics runs two computations over the same alarm and ticket data. The completeness path is a nightly Spark job over the whole retained history in Iceberg: it recomputes, per circuit, the full service-level attainment - time in outage, missed restoration targets, credit owed - and republishes an immutable partition for every circuit and month. The freshness path is a .NET 8 worker fleet consuming the alarm stream from Kafka; it keeps only the current incident state and the last hour of transitions per circuit in a serving store, because a five-minute-old answer is worthless on the operations bridge. The query API answers a dashboard by taking the settled partition for closed months and overlaying live state for the open period. The seam that keeps breaking is the record shape: the batch side reads Parquet rows with twelve fields in one order, the live side writes a compacted topic record with eight fields under different names, and three ad-hoc mappings now disagree about how a cleared alarm is represented. Neither representation may be forced to change for the other, yet every consumer must go through one translation. What should own that translation?

state: A network service provisioning product is one Spring Boot application: a single jar that drives the order workflow, submits activation requests to three carrier APIs, and serves the provisioning console, with one PostgreSQL database. It is deployed as one unit; the console and the carrier submission loop are the same release, restarted together, and no separate coordination process exists. A provisioning order is a cluster of rows - the order root, its circuits, its VLAN assignments, its maintenance windows and its carrier references - and they must change as a set: rescheduling a window while a circuit is mid-activation corrupts the assignment. The console keeps an edit session open for minutes while an engineer negotiates with the carrier, and two engineers on one order currently interleave writes because each row is locked only while written. The team wants one lock for the whole cluster, taken on the order root (a lock row keyed by the root id, or a token the root carries) so a caller locks one thing instead of discovering every member. The argument is granularity: one lock per order root serializes unrelated circuits, while per-circuit locks let the set drift. They also need a policy for lock duration, session loss and the nightly batch importer that touches 400 orders.

state: A Java claims-adjudication codebase represents an assessment in one mutable class with a status enum and eleven nullable fields: approved amount, deduction reasons, regulation clause reference, missing-evidence list, deferral deadline. Because every field exists on every status, defensive checks proliferate — 'denied outcomes must carry no approved amount', 'an approved outcome must carry at least one payable line' — and 340 stored rows violate them. The proposal fixes the alternative shapes in the type system: a sealed interface declares the complete set of outcomes, and one immutable record per outcome carries exactly its fields — approval the payable amount, partial approval the deductions, denial the regulation clause, deferral the missing evidence and deadline. Construction goes through the record's canonical constructor only, so an outcome that is denied and also paid cannot be written down. Constraints: the SQL layer must round-trip all four cases through one table via a type token and per-case payload; every case analysis in reporting must be re-checked by the compiler when a fifth case appears; no field may become nullable as a shortcut for absent data; and the records must stay usable as fee-ledger map keys.

state: A network service provisioning platform in TypeScript turns customer orders into configured optical circuits. The work runs as a chain of stages over an order stream: an intent stage parses the order into requested endpoints and bandwidth, a feasibility stage checks path and spectrum availability, a configuration stage pushes device configuration to the optical line system, and a verification stage reads back alarms and light levels. Each stage is a worker on its own thread with its own bounded queue, holds no reference to the others, and the verification stage can be detached to run minutes later against the same order value. The constraint is physical: each optical line system accepts at most eight concurrent configuration sessions before its management plane starts dropping NETCONF replies, and there are four line systems in the estate. We want a fixed pool of permits per line system, where a stage acquires a permit before it touches that device and releases it on every exit path, including abandoned and failed pushes, so at most eight sessions exist at once and a waiting stage blocks rather than being dropped. Constraints: 2 000 orders a day, no session leak across a deploy, and per-device limits configurable.

state: An editor extension managing infrastructure-as-code parameter files hosts several document sessions at once: files can be open in split panes, each bound to a session object tracking cursor, selection and a parsed model, and two panes sometimes share a file because it was opened twice. Each session keeps its own copy of the parsed model today; when two copies are edited they are written one after another and the last write wins, so a rename in one pane disappears when the other saves. The redesign multiplexes sessions over one shared model per file: opening the same file twice returns the same model object to both sessions, each edit goes into a pending-change list keyed by the model object rather than the session, and a save at the session boundary flushes every pending change for the affected files in one ordered pass, coalescing repeated edits to the same key. Constraints: closing one pane must not discard the other's pending edits; an undo must reverse exactly that session's last change although the list is shared; a failing flush must leave the model untouched and name offending keys per file; and the extension's own write must not be mistaken for an external change by the watcher, since the code runs inside the editor's extension host with no other process to coordinate with.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A turbine manufacturer runs a prediction service that forecasts blade degradation for 6,200 turbines under warranty. Vibration and thermal telemetry is featurised hourly; a survival model and a gradient-boosted classifier are retrained quarterly on inspection outcomes, validated on a fleet-disjoint holdout, and registered with the data snapshot and code commit that produced them. Serving emits a degradation forecast per turbine, and warranty engineers act on it: a predicted failure within 30 days triggers a site inspection. Because those inspections cost 40,000 euros each and the manufacturer bills the operator for missed ones, both sides' contracts name the forecast as the record of what was known and when. A dispute last year turned on whether a February forecast had been altered after the fact, and there was no way to show it had not. The service is C#, writes through a single logging chokepoint, and must now make its records verifiable: each entry chained to its predecessor so that altering, deleting, reordering or truncating the log is detectable by the operator's independent verifier, which reads only the log and a published head digest. Constraints: 20,000 entries a second, no more than 2 ms added at p99, entries produced by three services sharing one verifier contract, and five-year retention. Decide how the record chain and its verification are built.

state: A tax-preparation provider computes refund-risk and deduction-eligibility predictions for nine million filers each season. state: A Kotlin module in a video catalogue codebase passes one carrier object, RightsEnvelope, through several internal collaborators on every playback authorisation: ingest fills it, the rights resolver adds the entitlement decision, the audit writer records it. state: A C++ municipal waste-collection codebase models a collection round with a RoundPlan class that owns its stop sequence, its bin-load estimates and three nested index types used to address stops. state: Wexford University enrols 30,000 students. Four small applications, each with a private database, own pipeline and release cadence: `course-catalogue` (PostgreSQL, weekly), `enrolment` (PostgreSQL, daily, scales on the enrolment burst), `timetable` (PostgreSQL, weekly) and `tuition-billing` (PostgreSQL, monthly). Each owns its schema; `enrolment` reads course data over gRPC, each application scales on its own metric, and no application reads another's tables. Inside `enrolment`, a registration is a business transaction over three database transactions: check the seat count, reserve a seat, confirm the enrolment, with a payment authorisation between the last two. Holding a database lock across the payment call is not allowed because the provider can take eight seconds, and seats were oversold when two students raced. Decide the guarantee: each read record's revision is re-checked at commit, and the business transaction aborts and retries if any of them moved, so a long business transaction spans several short database transactions without a held lock. Constraints: 4,000 registrations a second at the term-start burst, a retry budget of three, no oversold seats, and the payment authorisation must not repeat on retry.

state: An electric vehicle charging operator runs one Go service: a single binary that terminates the OCPP websocket connections from 4,000 charge points, exposes the driver app's start and stop API, and reconciles sessions with a roaming partner, all in one process with one PostgreSQL database. state: A wholesale distributor's replenishment planner is a single C++17 executable: one native binary that loads the item master, runs the nightly reorder calculation, and serves a small status page to the operations desk. It runs on one on-premises server and is upgraded by replacing that binary; the whole planner restarts as one process. They must decide whether the holder is per-planner or per-policy, and whether the two other bases wanting the item master deserve the same treatment.

state: A container terminal runs crane and straddle-carrier control on servers inside the terminal, where a command must reach a machine within 30 milliseconds and must keep working when the terminal's link to the internet is cut; booking, invoicing and customer notifications run in one public cloud region. Booking confirmations arrive from the cloud and are applied by the on-premises gate controller, which also services driver check-ins at the gate lane. The controller may accept a booking change only when its own state is ready: the lane must be idle or assigned, the equipment's last command must be acknowledged, and the berth window must still be open. Today the controller waits on a condition for up to two seconds and then queues the change, which has twice let a straddle carrier receive a re-aimed move mid-cycle. The team wants the attempt decided at one instant: test the guard, apply the change only if it holds, and otherwise return an explicit refusal to the cloud within five milliseconds so the booking service can re-offer the slot. No waiting, no queue, no partial mutation, and the driver at the lane must get a printed reason.

label: security-verification

state: A university enrolment platform in Rust runs section availability as a fleet of long-lived Actix workers across four operating-system processes: each section is one worker with its own mutable state — capacity, waitlist order, prerequisite gates — and every request reaches it as a message through its address, handled one at a time, with the runtime restarting a panicked worker and rebuilding its state from the registrar's Postgres store. Every worker runs the same outer loop, the same admission throttle and the same metrics hook, but the shared code must call back into that worker's own message handler. The design choice under review is how to write the shared shell. One option parameterises it on the concrete worker type, so the loop is generated for that type and every callback resolves directly, with no vtable and no boxed trait object per message; the other stores a boxed handler and pays an indirect call on every message. The chosen shell must not force the concrete workers into an object-safe subset of their vocabulary, and the compiler must be able to inline the handler into the loop at the call sites it can see. Which shape?
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A forty-property hotel group keeps reservations in one Postgres cluster. At run time each reservation is one Elixir process on a three-node cluster, registered under the booking reference in a shared name registry, holding the row's current fields — arrival, departure, rate code, guarantee, folio flags, cancellation window — in its own process state. Commands arrive as messages from the front-desk app, the channel manager and the housekeeping board, and the process applies them one at a time: it re-checks the row-local rules (early arrival permitted, deposit required inside seven days, no downgrade after check-in) and writes the whole row back through Postgrex before replying. A booking reference has exactly one live process; after a crash the supervisor starts a new incarnation, which reloads the row by primary key. The team deliberately keeps the domain small: no detached domain objects, no separate mapping assembly, no repository layer. Two designers disagree about whether this shape is safe — one wants the SQL moved out so the process holds no storage code, the other says the row, its rules and its find and save belong on one unit. Which shape should ship?
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A streaming catalogue keeps, per genre shard, an in-memory index of every title's segment descriptors. At run time twenty-four Go shards spread over four worker processes each own one index, fed by a buffered inbox channel, handling one message at a time and answering lookups on a reply channel; a monitor goroutine restarts any shard whose handler panics and reloads that shard's index from the catalogue store. Each index is a slice of descriptor structs built by appending during the nightly ingest and then heavily pruned when a licensor withdraws a catalogue: one point two million entries can drop to ninety thousand inside an hour. Three months in, the process' resident memory sits four gigabytes above what the surviving entries need, because deletion only shortens the slice — the old backing array stays allocated and reachable, and the descriptor structs still pin their strings. The fix must return that excess storage to the runtime once the shard has settled, without copying on every deletion, and without handing out an array that another shard iteration can still append into.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A tax-preparation vendor ships an office edition: a Kotlin/JVM service on a PC in each accounting office, holding that office's archive of client ledgers. Returns are computed on the office box rather than centrally, because an office archive is forty to a hundred and twenty gigabytes and the regulator forbids moving raw ledgers off the premises. For one client the return computation must scan that client's whole transaction history — three million rows in the largest case — to find deductible categories, but the box has four gigabytes of heap and a return must finish in two minutes. Materialising the ledger as a list, or as an eager filter chain that allocates a new list per step, dies with an out-of-memory error on the largest clients. The team wants the scan expressed as a source that produces one transaction at a time and suspends between them, so only the categories that survive the filter are held, totals accumulate as the scan runs, and per-transaction records are discarded as soon as they are consumed. The scan must be cancellable when the preparer reclassifies something mid-run.

state: An auction house runs live sales from eight salerooms, each with a rostrum console and a clerk's station. Each lot's record is a per-category shape: a painting carries provenance entries, condition-report attachments, exhibition history and a chain of owner transfers; a wine lot carries bottle counts, ullage notes and cellar provenance; a motor vehicle carries registration, mileage and service history. The console must accept bids, close the lot and print the buyer's slip while the auctioneer is live, over a saleroom network that shares a 4 Mbit line with the rest of the house, so the lot record is committed to the console's local store before anything is forwarded. Today the record is spread across twenty-three columns shared by all categories, fourteen of them null for any given lot, and adding a field for one category means a migration on every console and a release window the auction calendar does not allow. The proposal: keep the whole lot record as one document in a single column, versioned by a category tag, so its shape can evolve per category without touching the others, while bids and hammer price stay in queryable columns.

state: A national digital-identity scheme: eleven banks, a government registry and four wallet vendors anchor credential schemas and revocation entries on a Hyperledger Indy network, so a verifier can check an issuer's public definition without asking that issuer whether it still exists. Revocation tails are large and rotate weekly. The performance requirement is hard: 6,000 verifications a second per core in the gateway, and the profile benchmark showed a 34 percent penalty for virtual dispatch and per-call branching in this path. The team wants the operation selected while compiling, from the type of a small policy argument that names the scheme, so one generic template serves both profiles with no runtime test. The generic code must need nothing about a profile beyond the operations that profile supplies.

state: A clinical laboratory network's results analytics runs two computations over the same result data. The completeness path rebuilds nightly from every result ever released, producing a complete immutable view of each analyser's calibration-adjusted results, reference-range version and quality control position, and rewrites the partition the accreditation audit reads. The freshness path consumes analyser output from a message queue and keeps only results released in the last four hours and the instruments currently flagged. The clinician query API merges them: the rebuilt history for a patient's trend, the live window for today's result. The query service is a Python application on FastAPI, and the results store is a columnar database whose driver reports errors with numeric vendor codes, connection objects that must be returned in a particular order, and a dialect of its own for time bucketing. Today business handlers import the driver directly: a reference-range rule catches a vendor code by number, three handlers build time buckets with the dialect's syntax, and two of them leak connections when a validation fails early. Business code must speak in result, specimen and reference-range terms and never see the driver. What should sit in front of the store?

state: A telecom billing mediation platform is one Clojure service. Its rating core - rounding rules, off-peak windows, roaming zones, minimum-charge top-ups - contains no Kafka client, no JDBC and no file-format library; it declares the boundaries it needs: ChargeSource for inbound call records, SubscriberPort for plan and zone data, and ChargeSink for rated output. Adapters attach a Kafka consumer, a subscriber cache and a partitioned Parquet writer, and the source adapter can be replayed from a fixture file in tests. The recurring problem is that the individual transforms - parse the record, drop duplicates, attach the zone, apply rounding, add the minimum charge, drop gone subscribers - are written as separate loops, so each materialises an intermediate sequence of two million records and each applied separately to the Kafka and replay paths. We want to express each transform once as a value that takes a step-combining function and returns one, compose the whole stack once, and then apply that composed value to either source and either sink, with the transform not knowing which it is attached to. Constraints: 12 million records an hour, no intermediate collections larger than a partition, and the same composed stack must be reusable for the monthly reprocessing run.

state: Aster Tax's on-premise transmitter is `efile-batch`, one Spring Boot process on the operator's own host; a single deployable, no cluster. The chain is `AdminController` -> `BatchRunService` -> the `Return` and `SubmissionBatch` domain types -> `ReturnRepository`, the only SQL. state: A Go codebase controlling warehouse robot fleets talks to PostgreSQL through database/sql only, with no mapper layer, and the inventory table has become the source of duplicated statements: eleven files contain their own SELECT ... FOR UPDATE over the slot table, five contain a hand-written UPDATE that disagrees about which columns are nullable, and the task allocator and the cycle-count job each implement their own insert with different conflict handling. The proposal gives each table row its own in-memory object mirroring the columns and carrying the row's own operations: an InventorySlot value holds slot id, aisle, level, sku, quantity, reserved quantity, version and last-counted timestamp, and exposes Find(ctx, id), Insert(ctx), Update(ctx) and Delete(ctx) methods that own the SQL for that table. Constraints: struct field names must stay the ones the allocator already compiles against; handling of the optional sku through sql.NullString must be decided once rather than per call site; Update must include the version column in its WHERE clause and report a stale-row conflict from RowsAffected; a row loaded by Find must be usable by the allocator without a second query; and the 40 existing call sites must migrate without introducing reflection-based mapping into this hot path.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A subscription-billing platform runs as an Orleans cluster: one billing-account grain per account holds the plan version, credit balance, dunning stage and invoice history in its own activation, and other grains can reach it only by sending a message to its account key. A grain processes one request at a time and nothing outside it reads its fields. Plans differ in what they allow — some accounts may take a mid-cycle plan swap, some support metered add-ons, a few support partial refunds — and the answer depends on the account's current plan version and standing, not on the grain class. The grain composing a credit note therefore has to ask the account, at the moment of the call, which of the optional contracts it actually honours. The reply must either be an endpoint the caller can immediately use for that contract, or an explicit refusal carrying a reason code, and a plan change that lands mid-flight must not leave a stale affirmative usable. Callers may not probe the account's concrete type, its deployment version, or a flag replicated through configuration.

state: A clinical trial runs fourteen sites; each site has a hub box beside the ward that collects vitals from sixty wearable and bedside devices, evaluates protocol alerts locally, drives a nurse-station display, and forwards to the sponsor's electronic data capture system nightly. The proposal: every state change produces a new complete snapshot and publishes it, leaving the previous snapshot untouched and available to whoever still holds it, with unchanged parts — device descriptors, protocol configuration — shared between snapshots rather than copied. No reader may see a half-applied update, and no reader takes a lock. What shape should the state take?

state: A container-terminal operator moves berth and yard instructions between a quay crane fleet, fourteen straddle carriers and a central planner over a lossy 4G link. Each piece of equipment runs an isolated service entity holding its own instruction queue and position state, handling one instruction at a time, addressed by equipment id; the planner never reads a carrier's state, it asks. The proposal: every payload names its own concrete shape through a discriminator the sending application adds, and the receiving entity resolves that through a registry of known concrete types before handing the decoded value to its handler, with a quarantine path for unknown discriminators so an old carrier never mis-decodes a new move. Which serialization shape?

state: A pharmaceutical cold-chain platform in TypeScript monitors shipments in transit. Temperature samples flow through stages joined by bounded queues: an ingest stage decodes logger packets arriving over satellite MQTT, an excursion stage evaluates each sample against the product's stability profile, a case stage opens and closes excursion cases, and a notify stage alerts the quality team. Each stage runs on its own worker with its own queue, holds no reference to another, and the excursion stage can be replayed over a stored shipment after a profile revision. The ingest stage multiplexes four hundred in-flight logger sessions over one upstream connection, and the gateway answers each read of a logger's configuration on the same connection, out of order and interleaved. Today the stage relies on arrival order, and a stability profile reached the wrong pallet twice in the summer. We want every outbound request to carry a unique token, the replier to echo that token in its answer, and the stage to match each answer to the request that caused it, so hundreds can be in flight at once with no per-request channel or session. Constraints: 40 000 samples a minute, answers arriving up to 90 seconds late, and a late answer for an abandoned request must be discarded, not misapplied.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A freight forwarder's transit-time platform forecasts arrival windows for 90,000 containers a week. A gradient-boosted model, retrained weekly on carrier-reported actuals, is registered with its feature definitions and served by a Java service that recomputes features from the same definitions, returning an arrival window with a 90% interval and the model version. Two pieces of state are shared: a per-lane calibration table (recent carrier performance by trade lane) read on every prediction and refreshed from a nightly batch, and a per-model cache of graph objects swapped when the registry promotes a version. Both are guarded by a ReentrantReadWriteLock held by hand-written code that takes the read lock at the start of the request method and unlocks at the end — and the batch refresh path takes the write lock inside a try block whose catch path never releases it, which caused a 40-minute stall last month when a carrier feed threw. The team wants lock lifetime bound to the scope of a block, so release happens on every exit path including exceptions and early returns. Constraints: 2 ms p99 on the prediction path, a Java 21 service, no reader starvation during the nightly refresh, and a registry swap that must not be visible to an in-flight prediction. Decide how the locks are acquired and released.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A vaccine cold-chain platform runs one Erlang/OTP process per shipment lane, spread over a three-node Erlang cluster. Each process owns that lane's sensor thresholds, excursion history and escalation state in its own heap and is reachable only through its registered name; no other process, on that node or the others, can read those fields. Temperature readings arrive in the process mailbox, and the process handles one message at a time — a reading, a timer tick from erlang:send_after, or a partner callback — so two readings can never interleave inside a lane's state. When the lane has to push an excursion notice to a partner's consignment API and the call fails, the scheduling of the next attempt is the open question. Attempts must wait a growing multiple of the previous wait, capped at ten minutes; the wait must carry a randomised spread, because forty lanes that lost the same partner would otherwise fire on the same second; and the sequence must be bounded by attempt count, elapsed time and a deadline carried on the original message. The pending schedule must survive a supervisor restart of the lane, which replays the lane's durable log and must not re-fire attempts already acknowledged.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: Copperfield Hotels runs four small applications for 1,800 properties, each holding a private database and shipping on its own cadence: `reservations` (SQL Server, deploys twice a week), `room-inventory` (SQL Server, daily, scales on request rate), `rate-plans` (PostgreSQL, weekly) and `guest-profiles` (Cosmos DB, monthly). Inside `room-inventory`, `RoomNightAvailability` is an in-memory dictionary of 60,000 room-nights rebuilt at start-up and refreshed by a background sweep at 02:00; the booking API reads and mutates it, and a nightly hold-expiry job also mutates it. Two teams wrote locking and non-locking variants, and a torn read on a busy date once oversold 12 rooms. Decide where the state lives: the dictionary and the single lock that serialises access live inside one dedicated object, and every read and write is a method on that object taking the lock, so no caller can reach the dictionary without it. Constraints: 500 concurrent requests, 60,000 room-nights, the 02:00 sweep must not starve the API, and the holder class must stay usable from an async handler.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A construction procurement portal is one Go binary: a single service that serves the bid submission pages, runs the tender-award batch, and generates the award notices, with one PostgreSQL database. It is deployed as one binary behind the office load balancer and restarted whole; the award batch is a subcommand of that binary, so both paths run the same build. Each HTTP interaction is currently one 200-line function: it parses form values, applies the award rules, and writes HTML, JSON or a PDF depending on the accept header. The PDF path was added last quarter by copying the JSON handler, and the two now disagree about who may award a tender when the bid bond is missing. The team wants each interaction split into three parts: a small handler object that pulls transport input and nothing else, a domain entry point that takes plain values and returns a domain result without seeing transport types, and a responder that turns that result into whichever representation the client asked for. Routing and cross-cutting dispatch stay outside the three. The questions are whether to have one handler object per route or per resource, whether the domain entry point returns a result value or signals a domain error, and how the PDF and HTML responders share layout without re-deriving the rules.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A pharmacy dispensing platform in Kotlin prints labels as prescriptions clear. Prescriptions flow through a chain of stages joined by bounded channels: an intake stage parses the electronic prescription, a screening stage applies interaction and dose rules, a composition stage produces the label content, and a dispatch stage sends it to one of three printer models. Each stage runs in its own coroutine on its own dispatcher with its own queue and keeps no reference to another stage. The label specification is immutable and has twenty-odd facts, of which a given pharmacy sets six or seven: patient and address flags, prescriber block, warning pictograms, font scale, barcode symbology, copy count, and a caution line from a regulatory set. Today the composition stage calls a constructor with twenty positional parameters, and two pharmacies got the wrong warning set because a null landed one position off. We want it assembled stepwise through named operations that can be called in any order, each setting one fact and returning the in-progress value, with a final operation that rejects missing mandatory facts. Constraints: three printer models, no nullable fields in the finished value, and the assembly protocol reused for a second product only if its steps match.

state: Forty freight forwarders, two ocean carriers and a customs broker record bills of lading and container releases on a Besu network with IBFT ordering; each forwarder runs a validator and holds the same replica, and no forwarder's operator can amend a released bill. Releasing a consignment is slow human work: a clerk opens it, checks the carrier's arrival notice, attaches the customs entry and the payment reference, and only then submits. The network operator wants a release to begin by taking an explicit claim on the consignment, persisted on the shared record and visible to every member, so once a clerk starts no other member can begin a conflicting release; the claim carries an owner, an expiry and a reason, and expiry returns the consignment to the pool. The team must decide where the claim is taken, what the network enforces versus the client, and how an abandoned claim is recovered without letting a member hold a consignment indefinitely.

state: An identity-verification provider runs document-checking kiosks in two hundred post offices. state: An agricultural sensor network turns soil-moisture telemetry into irrigation advisories. Readings flow through a chain of stages joined by bounded queues: a decode stage parses LoRaWAN frames into calibrated readings, a model stage computes depletion against the crop's root depth, an advisory stage decides whether to irrigate and for how long, and a publish stage sends the advice to the farm's dashboard. Each stage runs in its own thread, holds no reference to another, and the model stage can be swapped for a region-specific version without touching the others, which is how the vineyard model was introduced. Storage differs by deployment: each farm gateway runs SQLite on a device, regional aggregators run TimescaleDB, and the research replay runs Parquet files. The pipeline currently branches on deployment in four places to pick a driver. We want each deployment's wiring to construct one store-scoped object that owns the connection settings, dialect, pooling and migrations, and returns the matching family of access values - reading store, sensor store, farm store - built for that engine. Stages receive that family and never learn which engine answered. Constraints: 4 000 gateways losing connectivity daily, a new engine next season, and no conditional driver code outside wiring.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: An exchange's settlement platform evaluates fails-management clauses for equity trades. Operations staff author the clause set — counterparty tier, settlement cycle, partial-delivery tolerance, buy-in deadline, penalty band — in a decision-table console, and the compiled package is deployed to a settlement decision service that evaluates each open instruction against the day's positions and produces either a matched settlement or a fails case. About 1.4 million instructions are evaluated in the nightly cycle and again intraday on every amendment; clause changes ship as a data release reviewed by the operations committee. When an evaluation reaches a durable conclusion, four parties need to know: the custodian's back office, the clearing member's risk system, the regulatory reporting feed and the buy-in desk, each with its own processing, and none of them calls the settlement service, which must not gain a dependency on any of them. Today a nightly CSV drop serves three of the four, with a bespoke REST call for the fourth. The decision is what gets published when it does: what the item contains, what it guarantees about immutability and identity, and how a consumer that starts late can tell what it missed. Constraints: T+1 deadlines, a regulator that requires the published item to be replayable for five years, and consumers that must be addable without changing the settlement service. Decide the published item.

state: A retail chain runs point of sale in nine hundred stores. Each store's till server keeps the local sale journal and can complete a sale when the wide-area link is down, because the chain's agreement with its card processor accepts a two-hour offline window; the product catalogue, price book and chain reporting run in one public cloud region. Three store generations coexist: an old till server with SQL Server Express, a mid-generation with Postgres, and two hundred new stores on DynamoDB through a cloud gateway. The point-of-sale application is C# and is deployed to every store from one build. Today it branches on a store-type flag in eleven places to pick its own query code, and the DynamoDB stores cannot run the old SQL, so the branch has already been wrong twice. The team wants the persistence layer produced once per store from a single entry, reading which engine the till server actually has and returning a coherent set of handles — sale journal, price lookup, tender summary, offline replay — all bound to that engine and its dialect. Application code must never see a connection or a dialect string, and adding the fourth store generation must not touch the sale path.

state: Ridgeway Automation runs goods-to-person warehouses. Four applications, each with a private store and an independent release pipeline: `task-orchestrator` (PostgreSQL, daily, scales on open tasks), `robot-fleet` (Redis, on demand, scales per connected robot), `bin-inventory` (PostgreSQL, weekly) and `telemetry` (TimescaleDB, monthly). Each owns its data; the orchestrator calls `bin-inventory` over gRPC and commands robots through `robot-fleet`, and each application scales on its own metric. Inside `task-orchestrator`, every pick instruction passes four small validation steps: normalise the bin code, check the weight against the robot's payload, check reach against the aisle geometry, resolve the target slot. Each step is a pure function with one input and one output, but today they are called by hand in four places with slightly different orders, and one path skips the weight check for oversized items. Decide how the chain is expressed: combine the steps once into a single reusable function by sequencing them with a combinator, so the order is stated in one place, each step stays independently testable, and the combined chain is a value other code can pass around. Constraints: 700 robots, 40,000 picks an hour, a step is added most weeks, and order matters.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A coalition loyalty programme posts about six million ledger entries a night. Each entry is validated, translated into points by the partner's earn rule, converted into the member's currency, applied to the member's balance, and written to the settlement extract. One nine-hundred-line Kotlin function does all five inside a single coroutine, and the team cannot test or instrument the middle three. The redesign runs each step as its own resident coroutine with its own Channel acting as the inbox the previous step writes into: a step takes one entry at a time, keeps whatever it needs for itself — the current conversion table, the batch totals, the quarantine list — privately, and hands the result to the next step's channel. Steps are addressed by their channel and share no mutable state; the parent scope supervises them, so a failed step is restarted without discarding the other four. The requirement: the flow must read top to bottom as five named stages, each replaceable on its own — a second conversion stage for the Swiss partner, a no-op settlement stage in tests — and each runnable in isolation on a fixed sample. How should the work be decomposed?

state: A streaming service's catalogue platform decides what each title may be shown with. Editorial policy is authored as clauses — territory rights windows, content-rating ceilings by profile, licensing blackout dates, device-class restrictions, promotional overrides — about 2,500 of them in a rule editor, published as versioned data to a Go decision service that evaluates them for each catalogue request and returns the playable set for a profile. Clause changes never rebuild the service; the bundle is hot-swapped and every response records the bundle version for rights audits. The evaluation code, though, is tangled: the title type holds a pointer to the rights calendar, the calendar calls back into the rating policy, the rating policy needs the territory resolver, and the resolver imports the title package, so an import cycle is avoided only by a shared struct of interfaces. Unit-testing the rating logic needs five collaborating types and a fake clock. The team wants the one type that decides an effective rating band for a title in a territory to be constructible from its inputs alone, so its definition is the whole explanation of its meaning and a test needs nothing else. Constraints: clauses stay external data, evaluation under 5 ms at 30,000 requests a second, and the rights team owns its calendar on its own release schedule. Decide how that type is shaped.

state: An electric vehicle charging operator runs one Go service for session settlement. Its interior keeps settlement rules - idle-fee accrual, tariff step boundaries, roaming surcharges, refund eligibility - in structs and methods that import only the standard library; no MQTT client, no SQL driver and no HTTP package appears. The rules reach the world through three interfaces they define: SessionStore for sessions and meter values, TariffBook for the price schedule, and OutletCommand for unlocking a connector after payment. Adapters persist to PostgreSQL, read tariffs from the commercial team's API and send unlock commands over OCPP. Charge-point gateways, however, speak a publish-subscribe protocol: they publish meter frames on topics and expect session commands on other topics. Today a hand-rolled client inside the settlement code makes the rules know topic strings. We want the app left as it is and one endpoint component taking the client's role: it converts frames into calls on the store and the rules, and turns the rules' own notifications and commands into outbound channel operations, in both directions, reconnecting and re-subscribing on its own. Constraints: 9 000 charge points, gateways that reconnect hourly, and no protocol type may appear in the settlement package.

label: interaction-boundary

state: An identity verification service is one Spring Boot jar: one JVM serving the capture upload, the liveness challenge and the decision callback, with a single PostgreSQL database and one release cadence for all of it. The HTTP endpoints hand each verification session to one of eight long-lived worker threads that run the orchestration: fetch documents, run OCR, compare faces, write the decision. Nothing can be deployed per job type; the whole application restarts to pick up a model change. The session object holds an OCR scratch buffer, a mutable candidate list and a provider client that is not safe for concurrent use. Rather than lock it, the team wants the object reachable from exactly one worker for its whole life: created inside that worker, passed down ordinary method parameters, never published to a shared field, never captured by a lambda handed to another executor, and never returned to the HTTP thread. The hard part is the callback - the provider's asynchronous response arrives on a different thread and currently holds the session in its closure. They must decide how that response is re-queued back to the owning worker without leaking the reference, and whether a session may be retained between retries.

state: A container-repair network's analytics runs two computations over the same inspection data. The completeness path rebuilds monthly from every inspection and repair order ever recorded, producing a complete immutable view of bay throughput, rework rate and warranty exposure per depot, and rewrites the partition. The freshness path consumes inspection events from Kafka and keeps only current bay occupancy, queue length and today's completed units. The depot console merges the two: settled months from the rebuild, the live floor from the event path. The allocation engine is a Rust service on tokio. It shares one in-memory slot table across request handlers, and today a handler acquires a mutex, then calls into a helper that can fail or panics, and in two paths returns early before the unlock; after an unrelated panic last spring the table stayed locked until the process was killed, and every depot on that node stopped allocating. The lock must be acquired when control enters a region and released on every exit path, including early returns and panics, without relying on each author to remember it. What should the locking discipline be?

state: A charging-network operator runs nine hundred AC and DC sites. Each site has a local controller on the operator's own hardware, connected to the charge points over OCPP 1.6J and to the central management system over a mobile link that is down for minutes at a time. A session start has to be decided on the site: the controller must confirm the connector is free, that the site's transformer allocation can absorb the requested power, and that no other session is being started against the same feeder, all before the first kilowatt-hour flows. Today it checks these by reading, then writes the session, and during a reconnect storm last August two sessions started on one feeder and tripped the site breaker. The redesign should make each start take a persisted claim on the connector and on its feeder share before any work begins, so a second start is refused at once instead of being discovered to conflict after the car is plugged in. The claim lives in the controller's local store, survives a reboot, and is released on session end, fault or operator command; the central system learns the outcome afterwards.

state: A contact centre routing platform in C# handles voice, chat and email contacts. Contacts flow through stages joined by bounded queues: a channel stage normalises each contact into a common envelope, a skills stage resolves required skills and language, a priority stage computes a queue position from contract tier and waiting time, and an assignment stage picks an agent and writes the reservation. Each stage runs on its own worker with its own queue, holds no reference to another, and the priority stage can be replaced with a simulation that replays a day's contacts without touching the others. That shape is being questioned because the assignment stage now needs three hundred lines and two developers want to introduce an agent-domain model. Constraints: 90 000 contacts a day, a two-second routing budget per contact, supervisors change priority rules weekly without a deployment, and a contact must never be assigned twice. state: A grocery retailer's replenishment platform predicts demand for 180,000 SKU-store pairs and emits nightly order proposals. Feature computation aggregates 104 weeks of sales, promotions and stockouts; a gradient-boosted model with per-category configuration is retrained weekly, validated on a store-disjoint holdout, and registered; serving recomputes features from versioned definitions and returns a forecast distribution and a proposed order quantity. Concurrency is guarded by one global lock around the cache, and at 4,000 requests a second with 32 workers that lock is the top of the latency profile: p99 is 45 ms against a 10 ms budget, and the profiler attributes 70% of the wait to cache access touching different keys. The team wants contention bounded by hashing keys onto a small fixed set of locks, so operations on different keys usually proceed in parallel and lock memory does not grow with the number of keys. Constraints: 180,000 keys, a 10 ms p99 budget, no change to the forecast model or its versioning, and a correct path when two workers touch the same key. Decide how the cache's locking is organised.

state: A health insurer's claims platform decides payment for 260,000 claims a day. A gradient-boosted model scores each claim for suspect billing, and a second model predicts the expected payable amount by procedure and geography; both are retrained monthly on adjudicated outcomes, evaluated on a locked holdout, and registered with the feature definitions they were trained against. state: A C# field-service dispatch codebase recomputes each technician's next job on a ten-second planning tick, and the route optimiser rewrites the same technician's status five to forty times inside one tick as constraints tighten. Each rewrite currently issues its own UPDATE through the repository, which saturates the connection pool at shift start and grows the audit table twelvefold without adding information. The team wants the in-memory view and the stored rows to decouple: a change list keyed by technician id keeps only the latest value per row, repeated writes collapse into one pending entry, and a single ordered flush at the end of the tick emits one parameterised UPDATE per technician inside one transaction. Constraints: a read from the optimiser during the tick must observe its own pending writes rather than the stale row; the flush must keep working when one statement fails, leaving the rest pending and the failed id marked; memory must stay bounded when a technician churns hundreds of times; and an interrupted flush must never write a value older than one already stored.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A pharmaceutical wholesaler's replenishment analytics is team-owned: batch and expiry records, supplier lead times, price schedules and depot stock each belong to the team that operates that part of the supply chain, are published with a schema and a quality expectation, and are rebuilt by that team's own jobs in Postgres and Iceberg; a platform group runs the object store, the catalog and the Trino endpoints, and none of the planning logic. The service's callers should be able to ask for a value on a given date the way they ask for any other field. What interface should those few fields present?

state: A container-terminal operator's analytics estate is owned team by team: berth planning, yard moves, gate transactions and customs release each publish their own datasets with a schema and a freshness target, and are rebuilt by the owning team's jobs in an Iceberg-on-S3 lakehouse, with a platform group running storage, the catalog and the Trino endpoints but none of it. Today every producer and consumer hand-rolls the translation and they disagree about how a missing location is encoded, so one consumer rejects messages another considers valid and the mismatch surfaces only in the partner's reconciliation report. Domain types must not learn the topic format, and the format must not leak into the domain. Where should the conversion live?

state: Northgate's enrolment platform puts a single registration endpoint in front of four backend capabilities: eligibility evaluation, seat allocation, fee assessment and document intake. Only that endpoint holds the public certificate and the partner rate limit; the four capabilities are internal and unreachable from the outside. A restriction is applied at the edge before routing: requests from the clearing house may only reach eligibility and document intake, and only with the fields their contract allows. Today the restriction guards only the first argument the edge deserialises and the first object it hands back, so a backend can return a nested reference that carries an unvetted capability or a callback the caller can invoke to escape the restriction entirely. The team wants a restriction that holds transitively: everything the backend receives and everything it returns, including nested objects, callbacks and lazily resolved handles, must already be constrained when it crosses the boundary, whatever the call path. The decision to make: how should the crossing between the edge and each backend be wrapped so an interface restriction applies to arguments, results, callbacks and nested objects alike rather than only to the first reference?
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A pathology network runs analysis instruments in thirty hospital laboratories. Each lab has a gateway box — an industrial PC on the lab's own bench network, bought and patched by the hospital's IT, not by the pathology network's platform team — running Azure IoT Edge with three .NET modules: one per analyser vendor protocol, one for result validation, one for the store-and-forward uplink. Instruments differ: some emit HL7 v2, some ASTM E1394, some a vendor binary, and three support an optional corrected-result callback while older units do not. The validation module must decide at run time, per connected instrument, whether an optional contract — corrected-result handling, or a bidirectional order fetch — is available, and must get back either something it can immediately send that contract's messages to, or an explicit negative it can cache for the session. It may not branch on module version strings, class names or deployment ids: labs are upgraded one box at a time and the version metadata has been wrong twice. Validated results must leave the box within thirty seconds, buffering locally while the link is down.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: An airline crew rostering service is a single Rust binary: one executable that stores crew qualifications, builds monthly rosters, and serves the crew portal, with one PostgreSQL database. It ships as one artifact and the process restarts whole; the roster builder is a code path inside the same binary, not a separate deployment, and a release moves generation and portal together. Every operational fact in rostering has a bounded life: a pilot is type-rated on the A320 from March to September, restricted to no night landings for six weeks after an incident, and qualified as a check airman only while a currency window is open. The schema stores valid_from and valid_to on some tables and nothing on others, so the builder falls back to updated_at and treats whatever is current in the row as true for the whole month it is planning. Last month that scheduled a pilot onto a redeye eleven days after the night-landing restriction started. The team wants every such fact to carry an explicit range of dates, and every reader to ask whether the fact holds on the roster date and get a defined answer. Decisions: whether ranges are half-open, whether a correction edits a range or appends a new one, and how the builder queries as-of dates in one pass.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: A grid operator's telemetry platform is a .NET service that streams synchrophasor and SCADA frames through four successive stages fed by bounded channels: a decode stage turns frames into typed samples, a quality stage marks stale or implausible values, a window stage aggregates one-second windows, and a publish stage hands each window to registered analysers. Each stage runs on its own thread with its own queue and shares no mutable state with the others, so the window stage can be moved downstream of an extra filter, and a new analyser is a package added at start-up rather than an edit to the chain. Analysers are third-party code from three vendors, and they are given a capability object to reach the platform's services: historical queries, alarm raising and a clock. Today every capability crossing the analyser boundary must be wrapped, including arguments passed in, callbacks and results handed back, so that a restriction applied to the interface is enforced transitively instead of guarding only the first reference, and the whole wrapped set can be revoked when an analyser is unloaded. Constraints: 30 analysers, one process restart a month, and a revoked analyser must not keep firing alarms.

state: A points engine inside a TypeScript loyalty-programme codebase still decides earning with a thick if-ladder in the checkout module, and the same four checks are copied into the campaign simulator and the yearly statement builder, where they have drifted. The rules are plain business facts: the member tier must be gold or above; the basket subtotal must clear a campaign threshold; the product category must appear on the campaign's list; the purchase date must fall inside a window. Each rule should become a small named object with one isSatisfiedBy(candidate) method, built by constructors such as minTierRule and categoryInRule, and combined by and, or and not helpers that return new rule objects rather than mutating any. The composed object is then applied by whatever code needs it, and unit tests exercise the rules against ledger fixtures with no basket, campaign or statement code present. Constraints: a statement run evaluates the composed rule against roughly 400 baskets, so each combination must be cheap; a composed rule must not capture a campaign snapshot at construction time, because the promotion end date changes during the run; and a failing rule must be able to say which named rule rejected the basket.

state: An electric-vehicle charging network's analytics is split among team-owned datasets - session telemetry, tariff schedules, charger asset health and payment settlement - each published with a schema and a freshness target and rebuilt by the owning team's own dbt or Flink jobs on Iceberg. state: A Kotlin grocery-delivery codebase books a delivery slot by constructing a SlotBooking that must carry a customer, a verified address, a slot window chosen from that address's zone, a substitution policy and an authorised payment intent. Two dependencies are ordered: a slot cannot be chosen before the zone is known, and authorisation cannot be taken before the basket price is final. Today a nine-parameter constructor with defaults and a copy method lets a caller build a booking from another zone's availability list or with payment attached to an empty basket; two such bookings reached drivers last month. The proposal constrains construction with types instead of validation: a first stage holds nothing and exposes only forCustomer(...), which returns a customer stage; that stage exposes only deliverTo(...), which returns a zone-resolved address stage; only that stage offers the slots of the resolved zone; authorisation appears only after pricing; and only the last stage declares build(). Constraints: exactly one reachable path from start to a constructed booking; a slot list from another zone must be unnameable at the type level; rebuilding a booking from a stored row must bypass the chain through a separate internal path; and reflection is unavailable on the target platform.

state: A workshop diagnostics service is a single Rust binary: one executable that reads OBD-II frames from a serial adapter, decodes them, and serves the technician's tablet over a local HTTP endpoint. Decoding, session logging and the tablet API all live in that binary, which ships to garages as one artifact and is restarted during service; the log writer cannot be upgraded without the decoder. Frames arrive as a set of variants the binary owns: P0301 misfires, P0420 catalyst efficiency, U0100 lost communication, extended manufacturer codes, and a raw frame, each carrying a different payload - cylinder number, freeze-frame snapshot, bus identifier. The current decoder walks the frame with if-let chains and a numeric range table, silently ignores unknown ranges, and reads freeze-frame fields with indexing that panics on the 2019 diesel profile. The team wants every handler - decode to display text, decide whether the fault blocks the vehicle, build the workshop report line - to take the variant apart by structure and bind its payload in one expression, with the compiler rejecting a handler that forgot a variant. The question is whether to keep one central match per handler or attach the behaviour to the variants, given that the report format changes monthly.

state: Metroline charges fares for 4 million journeys a day. Four applications, each with a private database and its own deployment and release schedule: `fare-ledger` (PostgreSQL, weekly, scales on journey rate), `ticket-issuance` (PostgreSQL, daily), `validator-network` (PostgreSQL, on demand, scales per active gate) and `refunds` (PostgreSQL, monthly). Constraints: 4 million journeys a day, schema changes every sprint, no ORM available for the chosen driver, and capping must stay unit-testable without a database.

state: A C# network-provisioning codebase stores a subscriber circuit as five tables: the circuit, its line termination, VLAN assignment, bandwidth profile and activation window. The dependent rows mean nothing apart from the circuit, are always created and retired with it, and are never referenced by id elsewhere — yet every caller assembles and persists them separately, and the provisioning console's update path has produced two circuits whose bandwidth profile belongs to a different VLAN because the writes were not ordered. Four applications, each with a private data store, pipeline and release: `observation-ingest` (TimescaleDB, on demand, scales on station count), `model-runner` (S3 output grids plus PostgreSQL run metadata, two runs a day, monthly deploys), `forecast-api` (PostgreSQL plus Redis tile cache, daily, scales on request rate) and `alerting` (PostgreSQL, weekly). Each owns its data; the API reads grids from S3 by run id and never reads another application's tables, each scales on its own metric, and clients call `forecast-api` directly. Inside `forecast-api`, a new model run sometimes lands 90 minutes late, and the renderer producing ensemble percentile tiles can also fail on its own. Today a late run or a dead renderer turns the whole response into a 500 and the public status page shows an outage, although the deterministic surface fields from the previous run are still cached. Decide the behaviour: detect the missing dependency, serve the last complete run with its issue time, drop the optional ensemble layers, and label the response as partial rather than failing it. Constraints: two runs a day, 14-day retention, a public SLA, and meteorologists who must see which run answered.

state: A fuel-card processor settles forecourt transactions from two thousand two hundred sites. Each site controller accumulates completed transactions — pump, shop, car wash — during the day and pushes them to the processor over a link that is metered, sometimes 2G, and occasionally lost for hours. A batch for one site can hold four hundred transactions and two megabytes, so it is cut into parts, and the processor must know a batch is whole before it posts the settlement, because a partly posted batch produces an unbalanced daily position that finance then chases for a week. Today the parts carry only a batch id and the processor guesses completeness from a ninety-second quiet period, which fails whenever the link is slow; two sites were double-posted last quarter. The team's rule: every part is stamped with a batch identity, its position in the batch and the total count; the receiver reorders by position, holds parts until the count is reached or a declared end marker arrives, detects gaps and asks for the missing positions by number. The site controller decides the batch boundary, on count or on age.

state: An industrial maintenance platform predicts remaining useful life for 30,000 assets. Sensors stream vibration, temperature and current; a Python feature service computes rolling statistics; three models — bearing wear, lubrication breakdown, motor insulation — are retrained weekly on work-order outcomes, validated against an engineer-reviewed holdout, and registered with the feature-code hash they were fitted on. Serving recomputes features from the same code and returns a remaining-life estimate with a confidence band; a monitor tracks error against actual failures. Maintenance engineers configure each asset's degradation expression themselves in a small expression language, for example min(rolling_mean(vibration, 7d) / baseline, 1.0) * wear_weight + startup_cycles / 1000, because bearing geometry and duty cycles differ per asset class and the engineers refuse a fixed formula. Today those expressions are evaluated by a growing chain of ad-hoc Python callbacks registered in a dict: an invalid expression is discovered only at evaluation time, the grammar is documented in a wiki, and two engineers' expressions behave differently for the same text. The language is small — literals, sensor references, arithmetic, comparison, a conditional, about a dozen functions. Expressions are stored as validated text per asset, versioned with the model registration they were tuned against. Constraints: 30,000 assets every five minutes, no dynamic code execution allowed by security review, and new functions addable by the platform team. Decide how the language is represented and evaluated.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: Northgate Lending processes 4,000 mortgage applications a day. Four small applications, each with a private store and its own deployment pipeline: `application-intake` (PostgreSQL, daily, scales on intake rate), `document-verification` (S3 plus PostgreSQL, weekly), `underwriting` (PostgreSQL, weekly) and `offer-generation` (PostgreSQL, monthly). Each owns its schema; underwriting receives a packaged application over gRPC, each scales independently, and no application reads another's tables. Inside `underwriting`, a case carries up to 30 conditions, and three separate code paths walk them: the eligibility check, the exception writer and the broker summary. Each path computes indices, checks bounds and dereferences, and one skipped the last element twice because of a `<` versus `<=`. Decide how the walk is expressed: the collection type gets responsibility for walking itself and accepts one caller-supplied action per element, so clients stop computing indices and checking bounds and the traversal is written once. Constraints: 30 conditions per case, three call sites, a broker summary that must keep its original ordering, and an exception writer that may mutate each element it visits.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: An auction platform's bid-integrity system scores every bid for shill-bidding risk. Features aggregate bidder-graph structure, device fingerprints, bid timing and price ladders; a graph model and a gradient-boosted model are retrained nightly on confirmed enforcement cases, approved by a trust-and-safety reviewer, and registered with the graph snapshot they were built on. Serving scores bids in a Kotlin service as they arrive, writing a risk score per bid, and the enforcement console reads those scores and updates a bidder's status when a case opens or closes. The bidding path is the hottest in the company — 55,000 bids a second at peak on closing nights — and the score writer issues one UPDATE per scored bid plus one per status change, so the PostgreSQL primary runs at 70% CPU on single-row writes, and the closing-night spike has twice pushed replication lag past the point where the console shows stale statuses. Almost all writes touch a small working set: 3,000 live auctions, and repeated status flips of the same bidder within a session. The team wants changes accumulated in memory and flushed as coalesced batches at a boundary, so intermediate states never reach the database and repeated writes to a row collapse into one statement. Constraints: a 200 ms bid acknowledgement, no lost score on process crash, and a read path that must keep seeing committed state. Decide how score and status writes reach the store.

state: A Java claims-adjudication codebase derives each claim's payment plan in two passes: one function expands the claim's terms — award date, instalment count, indexation rule, partial-settlement credits — into dated instalments, and a second folds that list into the figures the adjudicator sees: total payable, present value, first and last payment dates, suspended count. Across a nightly batch of 400,000 claims the intermediate lists cause most allocation churn, and one path has already kept a list alive across a transaction boundary. The proposal fuses the two passes: one recursion carries a seed describing the remaining terms and an accumulator describing the folded result, each step producing the next seed with its contribution or terminating, so the intermediate structure is never materialised. Constraints: the fused totals must match the two-pass version to the cent on the 5,000-claim regression set; the step must not grow the JVM stack without bound on a 360-instalment mortgage claim, so the driver loops over an explicit step value rather than recursing; suspension handling must skip a step without dropping its date from the folded range; and an auditor who does not know the fusion must still read it, which argues for naming the seed and the step rather than nesting lambdas.
instructions: Which design-pattern category does this decision belong to?

state: Six grid operators meter settlement data on a shared network where each operator holds a replica and an endorsement from three of the six is required before a reading becomes final. Forty thousand smart meters per minute arrive at a single ingest application run by the network operator, which validates, batches and submits proposals, then waits for commit. The design must bound each member's in-flight work separately, state what happens when a member's share is exhausted (queue with a deadline, or reject early), and keep the totals inside the node's memory and file-descriptor budget. state: A litigation support product used by two law firms is one Java 21 service process. Its interior holds a review core - classes that decide privilege risk, responsiveness and redaction duty from a document's text and metadata - and that core imports no Spring, no JDBC and no PDF library. It reaches everything through boundaries it declares: ClausePort for extracted passages, PrivilegePort for the firm's privilege register, RedactionPort for producing redacted derivatives, and WorkProductPort for the review set. Adapters implement those against a PDFBox-backed extraction store, the register's REST API, an image redaction service and the review database, and each is replaceable with fixtures in the rule tests. Thirty review operations exist today and one arrives most months. Every operation needs the same protected steps - pull a passage, take a risk score, write an annotation, check the register - and each currently reaches the extraction engine and the register adapter directly. We want the engine and the register touched only in one base class that exposes those steps to its subclasses, with each operation living in its own subclass out of them. Constraints: outside counsel must not see other matters, and a review run of 400 000 documents must not re-enter the register.

state: A construction procurement platform is one .NET 8 service process. Its interior splits the same way everywhere: a framework-free bid-evaluation core - deadline arithmetic, sealed-bid opening order, arithmetic-error checks, abnormal-low-bid tests - and boundaries the core declares for everything outside, BidSheetPort for the submitted sheets, SupplierScorePort for past performance, and ApprovalPort for routing an award. Adapters read SQL Server, a supplier rating API and an approval workflow, and the rating adapter is a stub in the core's test project. The core's readability has degraded in a specific way: its methods are dense with single delegated expressions - comparisons against the submission cut-off, membership tests on the sealed-bid list, arithmetic on the bid bond - repeated verbatim in several places. Two of those repetitions were corrected in one place and not the other, and a late bid was admitted last month. We are considering giving each of those single sends its own one-line, intention-named method so call sites read the intent and the expression exists once, and so the core's tests can target the named operation. Constraints: 300 tenders a year, the audit pack must show the rule text next to each decision, and no new dependencies in the core.

state: A building controls vendor runs a cloud service that computes climate schedules for 900 office buildings. Facility engineers at each site author occupancy and setpoint clauses in a web editor — floor, zone, weekday, holiday calendar, plant capacity, energy-price band — and the resulting set is published per building as a versioned package that a decision service evaluates every 15 minutes against zone sensor facts, producing setpoint commands for the building's BACnet controllers. Clause packages are data: an engineer can shift a floor's morning warm-up by 30 minutes and see it at the next evaluation, with no vendor release and no controller firmware change. Editing sessions are long: an engineer opens a building's clause set, changes twelve zones, previews the 24-hour schedule and saves. Two engineers editing the same building today overwrite each other's work at save time, and the losing edit is unrecoverable. The vendor wants concurrent work on one building refused up front, with a clear owner and a bounded lease, so nobody discovers a conflict after 40 minutes of editing. Constraints: a 15-minute evaluation cadence, an approval step before a package goes live, an edit session that may span a lunch break, and certification audit records of who changed what. Decide how a building's clause set is protected while an edit session is open.

state: A wholesale bandwidth provider rates and bills nine thousand circuits in eleven currencies. The rating engine runs in a public cloud region; invoice finalisation and the statutory invoice archive run in the provider's own data centre, because tax authorities require the invoice of record to be produced in-country. The rating engine computes prorated monthly charges, early-termination charges and credits, allocates a circuit's total across its cost centres and rounds to the currency's minor unit. Today an amount is a Python float and a bare string currency in two places, a decimal with a separate currency column in a third, and the nightly reconciliation between them has produced one-hundredth-unit discrepancies on three hundred invoices a month. Finance wants one immutable value that carries the amount and its currency together, owns rounding, proration and allocation, and refuses arithmetic between different currencies. It must survive serialisation into the cloud invoice request and back, must compare and sort deterministically, and must reject a currency code it does not know rather than treating it as a string.

state: A Java procurement model for construction materials stores agreed unit costs as effective-dated rows: each CostAgreement carries a material code, a valid-from date, a valid-to date and a unit price. Every consumer of the model reaches into the row store and searches it itself — the tender comparison report, the variation-order pricer and the three-year budget projection — and two of those call sites disagree about what happens on a date that falls in a gap between agreements. The team wants the cost to become an ordinary-looking attribute again: agreement.cost().on(LocalDate) returns the value in force at that instant, derived from the dated rows without the caller knowing a list exists, and setCost(from, Money) schedules a change from a future date while leaving earlier history addressable. Constraints: a cost report performs roughly 30,000 such lookups across 4,000 materials, so a linear scan per call is unacceptable; a date before the first agreement and a gap between agreements must each produce a defined outcome instead of a silent last-row fallback; and the budget projection must keep compiling unchanged.

state: A video streaming catalogue runs as one Go program: a single statically linked binary that serves the catalogue admin API, runs the nightly rights-window sweep and writes the compliance record, all inside one process. It is deployed by copying the binary to two hosts and restarting both; releases and capacity changes apply to the whole program, and the record writer cannot be restarted without the admin API going with it. Rights changes and takedowns must be provable afterwards: each record has to be cryptographically chained to the one before it, so deleting, reordering, truncating or editing a middle record is detectable by an outside auditor who holds only the latest digest. Today three packages open the record file directly and each formats its own line, timestamps come from whichever host handled the action, and a support script can rewrite an entry. The decision is how to funnel every security-relevant action - privileged logins, rights changes, takedown approvals, failed authorization - through one writer that owns ordering, HMAC keys and record framing, and where the verifier belongs relative to that writer.

state: A telematics provider ingests about 400 million position reports a day from 120,000 vehicles and runs a Go decision service that evaluates safety and compliance clauses: harsh braking, geofence exit, excessive idle, driver-hours breach. The clauses are written in GRL text by fleet compliance analysts, stored in a Git repository, and loaded into a grule instance at start-up and on a signed hot reload; a clause change is a pull request and a bundle publish, never a service rebuild. Each report is inserted as a fact together with the vehicle's driver assignment, the active geofence set and the last known odometer, and the actions append violations to a case table. Persistence is deliberately dumb: every statement that touches the position_report table lives in one Go struct whose methods take and return plain row structs, and no other package contains SQL for that table. The tension is that the actions want rich behaviour on the report — derived speed bands, geofence membership — while the gateway contract is rows in and rows out. Constraints: 40,000 reports a second, a 50 ms per-report budget for the whole evaluation, a nightly replay of the previous day against corrected geofence geometry, and an analytics team that reads the same table read-only. Decide where the table's SQL and its row shape live.

state: A warehouse robotics orchestration service is one TypeScript deployment on Node: a single process that assigns tasks to robots, tracks battery and charge cycles, and serves the supervisor console, with one PostgreSQL database. It is one image, one release, one restart; the assignment loop and the console cannot be deployed apart.
